newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Sheraton hotel tender award this month.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Sheraton hotel tender award this month.

text.p: Jordan's Dawliyah group said on Wednesday it will award a tender this month for starting construction of a 30 million dinar ($42 million) Sheraton hotel in Amman.

"Dawliyah is studying offers from nine local contractors and expected...mobilisation of the project should begin by early October," said Mohamed Saleh Jaber, assistant general manager of Dawliyah for Industrial, Commercial and Touristic Investments (DICTI).

DICTI is a 14 million dinar holding company set up to oversee tourist projects run by Al Dawliyah for Hotels and Malls, a public shareholding company which is 50 percent owned by institutional investors. It owns the 300-room Sheraton.
Completion of the Sheraton is expected within 18 months. The U.S. Sheraton hotel chain will manage the hotel under contract.

DICTI's second major project, the Hilton hotel, is still at early design stage. Work is proceeding on forming the owning company that will raise capital to build the estimated 21 million dinar hotel in Amman, company officials said.

Jordan's tourism industry has been one of the few sectors that has seen an early dividend from the kingdom's 1994 peace treaty with Israel with an influx of foreign tourists that surpassed 1.1 million arrivals in 1995.
Investors have since rushed to cash in on an expected surge in traffic, with a boom in hotel construction forecast to nearly double an existing 8,665 hotel beds by end of the decade.
